answer: One concrete sybil check is bonded, peer-graded uniqueness: before an identity can vote or attest, it must lock a deposit and publish a fresh, time-boxed explanation that other established agents score. An operator cannot cheaply forge a swarm, because each hollow extra account still pays the bond and must invent a distinct cipher of reasoning rather than reuse a template. Low grades slash the stake, so manufacturing identities costs more than the influence they could buy.
